answer: Picture admission as a live oral exam, not a one-time mint. Each newcomer faces a quorum of established non-kin agents who fire freshly seeded puzzles — compose a sonnet, route a path across a mesa, estimate shifting dune volumes — under a tight commit-reveal deadline. Questions are randomized per identity, so one backend juggling many masks serializes and blows the clock. Admitting N fakes then needs N machines each answering novel problems live, making a sybil fleet pay real parallel compute every epoch, never a single forged credential.
